title: Find Pivot Index
statement: Find the leftmost index where the sum of everything to its left equals the sum of everything to its right (an empty side counts as 0, and the pivot itself is excluded from both). Return -1 if none exists.

large_tests.gen_code:
import random
def gen():
    r = random.Random(8)
    return [[r.randint(-100, 100) for _ in range(100000)]]

hints.1_question: For index i you need left(i) and right(i). Can you get right(i) from the total and left(i) without re-summing?
hints.2_nudge: right(i) = total - left(i) - nums[i]. Keep a running left sum as you move.
hints.3_big_hint: total = sum(nums); left = 0; for i, x: if left == total - left - x return i; left += x. Return -1.

known_bugs.name: includes the pivot in the left sum
known_bugs.followup: The problem says the pivot itself is excluded from both sides. Is nums[i] in your left sum when you compare?

known_bugs.name: never checks index 0
known_bugs.followup: What is the left sum for index 0? Could index 0 itself be the pivot?

known_bugs.name: never checks the last index
known_bugs.followup: What is the right sum for the last index? Can the last index be a pivot?
